newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 2.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI
--Yesterday's sale of treasury bills and bonds raised a record 800 billion drachmas for the finance ministry.
-- Deputy Commerce Minister Mihalis Chrysohoidis will meet with the Association of Greek Banks tomorrow to discuss the legislative framework governing the use of credit cards.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis is expected to reiterate to a leading European unionist tomorrow his recent positions on labour relations, which yesterday drew criticism from 300 ruling PASOK0-aligned unionists.

--The scalpel will cut deep into spending by public utilities and organisations (DEKOs) as the finance ministry plans to restrict credits for lending even if it means DEKOs having to fall back on exploiting assets to service their debts.
IMERISIA
--Yesterday's record amount of 800 billion drachmas has raised the tempo in the market, creating new conditions for a further fall in interest rates by the state and by private banks.
--A senior executive at a major insurance company will be prosecuted for the alleged sale of confidential client lists to a foreign firm.
--International tenders for the appointment of managing directors of six DEKOs in the transport ministry will go ahead soon.
KERDOS
--Sources say the government is ready to implement a series of reforms that will change the way the consumer price index is calculated and bringing inflation down by 1.0-2.0 percent.
--The Egnatia Bank is determined to enter the race to buy the Bank of Central Greece, according to reports.
--The repayment bill for DEKO loans in 1996 came to 118 billion drachmas, prompting the government to begin instituting a strict disciplinary code for those responsible.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Increased fluidity in the market, combined with the Bank of Greece's interventions, supported yesterday's issue of treasury bills and zero coupons, which overshot targets by 400 billion drachas.
--The Greek National Tourism Organisation is expected to soon announce a tender for the exploitation of a number of properties worth a total of 23 billion drachmas.
EXPRESS

--A foreign house to report on a possible solution to the relations between the Commercial Bank and its subsidiary Ionian will have been appointed by the end of the month as Ionian prepares to announce low profits for 1996. Commercial however will present profits of 13 billion, the only state-run bank to do so.

--Increased competition due to the full deregulation of the air transport market will force Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, to drop prices as it loses its monopoly over mainland Greece flights.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
